summary: A Workcell build round is currently gated twice over: `skills/build/scripts/waves.py` selects only issues in the earliest unfinished declared wave, so one straggler holds back later issues whose own `dependsOn` are already merged, and everything after the builders — integration, then documentation — runs strictly serially. This milestone lands the four approved parallelization changes against the workcell repository itself: (1) dependency-gated selection in `waves.py`, with the ownership-overlap check moved from the declared wave to the whole candidate in-flight set and overlapping candidates deferred rather than dispatched concurrently; (2) `skills/new-feature/SKILL.md` step 5 dispatching the `documenter` alongside the `integrator` instead of after the merge; (3) an explicit, opportunistic allowance in `skills/build/SKILL.md` for speculative next-wave `specifier` dispatches while the integrator runs; (4) a granularity rule for `ownershipHint` in the planner's sidecar contract, with a mechanical check so a hint is one path or glob rather than prose. What stays serial is stated and untouched: `specifier` -> `builder` per issue, the integrator's serial merge, nothing merging before combined GREEN, and the two-phase seal. Assumptions taken rather than asked: (a) `ownershipHint` keeps its string type — 'finer-grained' means a narrower glob and, where files span unrelated subtrees, more issues, not a list of globs; (b) a wave-0 overlap now defers the second issue instead of only warning and leaving it to hand-serialization, because the deferral machinery this milestone adds is exactly what wave 0 was missing; (c) the shipped offline dry-run keeps its outcome — the demo fixture still selects `API` and `UI` — and gains only the new `pulledForward` and `deferred` fields; (d) plan-time ownership-overlap detection inside `render_plan.py` is deliberately out of scope, because the glob matcher lives in `waves.py` and sharing it would couple two skills' scripts in a refactor nobody asked for.

architecture.changeSummary: This is a change to how one build round is scheduled, not to what a round proves. Today the orchestrator asks `waves.py` for the earliest unfinished declared wave, dispatches a specifier and builder pair per issue in it, waits for the integrator's combined run, merges, and only then dispatches the documenter — three serial stages after the builders, and a straggler in the current wave freezes issues that are already unblocked. After this milestone the selector answers a different question — which not-done issues have all their dependencies done — and resolves ownership collisions across the whole in-flight set by deferring a candidate to a later round instead of rejecting the plan or dispatching an overlapping pair. Documentation authoring moves beside the integrator rather than behind the merge, and the orchestrator may spend the integrator's idle time sealing next-round tests. The gates are untouched: overlapping work is never dispatched concurrently, a builder never starts without a seal, and nothing merges before combined GREEN.

issues.title: Dependency-gated wave selection with ownership deferral in waves.py
issues.body:
## Goal

Stop one straggler from freezing issues whose own dependencies are already merged. `skills/build/scripts/waves.py` currently selects "every unblocked, not-done issue in the earliest unfinished declared wave"; it must instead select every not-done issue whose `dependsOn` are all done, regardless of declared wave, and resolve ownership collisions across the whole candidate set by deferring rather than by rejecting the plan or dispatching an overlapping pair.

## Change 1 - `skills/build/scripts/waves.py`

In `derive()`:

- Build `ready`: every not-done issue whose every `dependsOn` entry is done (`is_done` is unchanged). Order it by declared `wave` ascending, then by sidecar order. Do not filter by `currentWave`.
- Walk `ready` in that order, keeping a selected list. A candidate whose `ownershipHint` overlaps the hint of an already-selected candidate (`globs_overlap`) is **deferred**, not selected this round.
- `unblocked[]` entries keep `key`, `number`, `ownershipHint`, `wave` and gain `pulledForward` (`true` when the issue's declared `wave` is greater than `currentWave`).
- Add top-level `deferred[]`: `{key, number, ownershipHint, wave, overlapsWith}`, in the same order, where `overlapsWith` names the already-selected issue key it collides with.
- `currentWave` keeps its present meaning and name: the earliest declared wave that still has an unfinished issue. It is reporting, not a filter.
- A declared same-wave overlap in a grouped wave (>= 1) stays a hard `BuildError`: the planner asserted parallelism the ownership hints cannot deliver, and that is a plan defect.
- Wave 0, the ungrouped bucket, keeps its single stderr warning naming both keys, and now **defers** the second issue of the pair instead of emitting both as concurrently dispatchable.
- The ordering matters and should be commented: earlier declared waves are selected first, so a deliberately coarse late hint (a whole-repository documentation pass, for example) defers itself rather than starving the issues it overlaps.

## Change 2 - `skills/build/SKILL.md`

- Wave-loop step 1: replace the "earliest unfinished declared wave" sentence with the dependency-gated definition, and say that `currentWave` still names the earliest unfinished declared wave for reporting and resume.
- Wave-loop step 2: the ownership check runs across the whole candidate in-flight set, not per declared wave; `waves.py` names deferred issues and the orchestrator dispatches them in a later round; overlapping work is never dispatched concurrently; a grouped-wave declared overlap is still rejected outright; the orchestrator may dispatch a subset of `unblocked` when it wants to cap concurrency, and pulled-forward issues are dispatched on the same base as the rest of the round and join the same integration round.
- Extend "Offline demonstration" with the second fixture command. A plain `python3 .../waves.py` block is safe; do **not** add a second `gh ... | jq` block - `test_documented_capture_command_produces_a_valid_snapshot` requires exactly one.

## Change 3 - fixtures (`skills/build/examples/`)

- Update `expected-waves.json` for the new fields. The selection outcome must not move: `unblocked` is still `API` then `UI`, both with `pulledForward: false`, and `deferred` is `[]`.
- Add `skills/build/examples/pull-forward/{plan.sidecar.json,issue-state.json,expected-waves.json}` covering both new behaviours in one plan: an unfinished wave-1 issue that no longer holds back a later-wave issue whose dependencies are done, and a ready candidate deferred because its hint overlaps a selected one. Its `planId` must differ from `builder-v3-demo`.

## Constraints

`skills/build/tests/test_build.py` and `skills/build/tests/test_skill_contracts.py` pin prose in this SKILL.md. Preserve these, verbatim:

- The canonical ADR-0007 orchestrator paragraph, still the second paragraph after the title.
- The single done-definition sentence: closed **and** (status:done or state_reason == completed), with its existing backticks and the reference to waves.py.
- The phrases: "GitHub is the source of truth", "current wave", "jj workspace", "combined GREEN", "sole completion authority", "force-push `main`", "at most twice", "stalled", "escalate to the human", "never dispatch a builder for an issue with no seal".
- The `## Single-PR mode` section, including "<planId>-integration", "agents/handoff.md", the `base` field, and "final PR from the integration branch to `main`".
- `Phase 1` before `Phase 2`.

## Verification

```sh
ruff check skills/
python3 -m unittest discover -s skills/build/tests -p 'test_*.py'
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 skills/build/scripts/waves.py skills/build/examples/plan.sidecar.json skills/build/examples/issue-state.json
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 skills/build/scripts/waves.py skills/build/examples/pull-forward/plan.sidecar.json skills/build/examples/pull-forward/issue-state.json
```

issues.title: Dispatch the documenter alongside the integrator in new-feature
issues.body:
## Goal

`skills/new-feature/SKILL.md` step 5 dispatches the `documenter` only after the wave has been integrated and merged, although doc authoring needs nothing but the changed-file and PR list, which exists the moment the builders finish. Move the dispatch beside the `integrator` and hold the landing, not the authoring, until combined GREEN.

## Change - `skills/new-feature/SKILL.md` step 5

Rewrite the step so it says, in this order:

- Dispatch the `integrator` over the wave **and** the `documenter` for whatever the feature changed about how the project is used, at the same time, on the same base, each in its own workspace (`workcell-ws add <name>`).
- The documenter's brief carries the changed-file and PR list and the docs-only `ownership` glob ([`agents/handoff.md`](../../agents/handoff.md)). Reading a file list or diffstat to choose a dispatch is orchestration under [ADR 0007](../../docs/adr/0007-primary-agent-is-a-pure-orchestrator.md); reading a file's contents to judge it is not.
- The documenter's `ownership` must be disjoint from every code issue's `ownershipHint`, so its branch can never collide with a builder's.
- Documentation never merges on its own authority. The docs branch merges only inside a combined GREEN that includes it: if the documenter returns before the integrator's serial merge begins, its branch joins that round and one combined run covers everything; if it returns later, dispatch one more `integrator` round over the docs branch on the merged base, and that round is also the docs gate (`skills/docs/scripts/docs_check.py`, plus `scripts/render-diagrams.py --check` where the README's visuals are generated).
- Nothing else moves: the wave's code PRs still merge on the integrator's evidence, and the final PR to `main` in step 6 is unchanged.

## Change - a home for this skill's contract tests

Create `skills/new-feature/tests/test_new_feature.py`. CI already discovers `skills/*/tests`, and `ruff check skills/` covers it.

## Constraints

- The canonical ADR-0007 orchestrator paragraph must stay the second paragraph after the title (`skills/build/tests/test_skill_contracts.py::test_orchestrator_boundary_is_canonical`).
- `single-PR mode` must still appear in this file (`test_build_defines_single_pr_mode`).
- The interview's "at least five clarifying questions" rule and the step numbering are untouched.
- This issue owns `skills/new-feature/**` only. `skills/build/tests/test_skill_contracts.py` asserts phrases about this file but belongs to another owner; if a change here would break one of those assertions, stop and escalate rather than editing it.

## Verification

```sh
ruff check skills/
python3 -m unittest discover -s skills/new-feature/tests -p 'test_*.py'
python3 -m unittest discover -s skills/build/tests -p 'test_*.py'
```

issues.title: Ownership hints are one narrow glob: planner contract and a mechanical check
issues.body:
## Goal

Coarse `ownershipHint` values are what force the build to serialize work that was planned as parallel, and the wave-0 bucket is where they collide most. Make the planner's contract say what a good hint is, and give the rule mechanical teeth for the one failure mode a machine can catch cheaply: a hint that is not a single path or glob at all. The shipped sample sidecar carries `templates/** and scripts/render_plan.py`, which every consumer - `waves.py`'s overlap check and the `ownership` field an agent is handed - treats as one literal path.

## Change 1 - `skills/planner/references/sidecar-contract.md`

State the rule where the planner agent actually reads it:

- `ownershipHint` is exactly one path or glob - a single token, never prose, a comma list, or two paths joined by "and".
- It is the narrowest glob that covers every file the issue changes **and the tests the `specifier` will write for it**, so place an issue's tests inside the subtree it owns.
- Hints must be disjoint within a wave; a collision is not merely untidy, it costs the parallelism the wave was for. `skills/build/scripts/waves.py` rejects a declared same-wave overlap outright and defers an overlapping candidate that it pulled forward.
- When an issue's files span unrelated subtrees, split the issue rather than widening the glob to their common parent. A pass that genuinely spans the repository (a documentation pass across `docs/`, the README, and the changelog) declares the common parent and, because a coarse hint overlaps everything, serializes itself.
- Give two worked contrasts: `skills/build/scripts/**` beats `skills/**`; root-level docs are `*.md`, not `**`.

## Change 2 - `skills/planner/SKILL.md`

One sentence in the plan workflow pointing at the rule, so the orchestrator reviewing a folio knows a coarse hint is a reason to send the plan back.

## Change 3 - `skills/planner/scripts/render_plan.py`

Extend sidecar validation: `issues[i].ownershipHint` must be a single token - reject any value containing whitespace or a comma, with a `PlanError` naming the issue index and the offending value and saying the field takes one path or glob. Nothing else about the field changes; it stays a required non-empty string.

## Change 4 - `skills/planner/examples/sample.sidecar.json`

Replace `templates/** and scripts/render_plan.py` with a single glob that covers that example issue's files and its `testPath`.

## Out of scope, deliberately

Plan-time ownership-overlap detection. The glob matcher (`generate_witnesses`, `path_matches`, `globs_overlap`) lives in `skills/build/scripts/waves.py`, which already imports the planner's validator; moving or duplicating it to run the check at render time is a cross-skill refactor that belongs to its own plan. Do not import `waves.py` from `render_plan.py`.

## Constraints

- Existing assertions in `skills/planner/tests/test_planner.py` stay green; the sample plans they build must satisfy the new rule.
- The canonical ADR-0007 orchestrator paragraph stays the second paragraph after the title of `skills/planner/SKILL.md`.
- This issue owns `skills/planner/**` only; the build-side fixtures and any other sidecar in the tree belong to other owners and already use single-glob hints.

## Verification

```sh
ruff check skills/
python3 -m unittest discover -s skills/planner/tests -p 'test_*.py'
python3 skills/planner/scripts/render_plan.py skills/planner/examples/sample.sidecar.json /tmp/sample-folio.html
```

issues.title: Permit speculative next-round specifiers while the integrator runs
issues.body:
## Goal

While the `integrator` runs the combined suite, the orchestrator has idle capacity and the next round's specifiers need nothing that does not already exist: they write failing tests and seal them. Write that allowance into `skills/build/SKILL.md` as an option with its cost stated, not as a default.

## Change - `skills/build/SKILL.md`, wave loop step 5

Add a short subsection ("Speculative specifiers", or equivalent) stating:

- While the integrator runs, the orchestrator **may** dispatch `specifier` agents for issues that will become ready once the in-flight set merges. They write the issue's `acceptanceTests` as failing tests on the current base, prove honest RED, and seal - exactly the standard Phase 1, nothing relaxed.
- It is opportunistic, never the default. The plain sequence stays correct and a run that skips speculation is not deficient.
- **Disqualifier**: an issue whose acceptance tests need the dependency's merged code to import or compile cannot be speculated. A test that cannot express its failure on the current base produces a hollow RED, and the `specifier` should return `blocked` rather than seal one.
- **Rework cost**: when a wave bounces - the integrator names an offending PR, a builder redoes work, or the merged base changes what the tests assume - the speculative seal has to be re-proved on the merged base and amended with `tdd-guard reseal --reason <text>`, and a re-scoped issue throws that specifier's work away entirely. The guard binds a seal to the sealed test files and the red command, not to the base it was proved on, so nothing mechanical catches a stale speculative seal: the discipline is textual and belongs here.
- **Never a speculative builder.** Phase 2 for a speculated issue starts only after its dependencies are merged, in a workspace on the merged base, and the builder re-proves the sealed tests still fail there for the right reason before implementing. If they now pass or fail differently, send the issue back to a `specifier` to reseal.

## Constraints

- Keep the wave loop's numbered steps and their order intact; add the subsection without renumbering.
- The canonical ADR-0007 orchestrator paragraph stays the second paragraph after the title; `Phase 1` still precedes `Phase 2`; the file keeps exactly one `gh ... | jq` capture block (`test_documented_capture_command_produces_a_valid_snapshot`).
- Do not weaken any existing sentence about the seal, the two phases, or merging on combined GREEN.

## Verification

```sh
ruff check skills/
python3 -m unittest discover -s skills/build/tests -p 'test_*.py'
```

issues.title: Record the overlap policy: ADR 0017, the how-work-moves diagram, README and changelog
issues.body: ## Goal One documentation pass that makes the repository's own account of the build loop true again, once the four mechanical changes have merged: an ADR for the decision, the generated README diagram, the prose beside it, and a changelog entry. ## Change 1 - `docs/adr/0017-the-build-wave-overlaps-where-the-seal-allows.md` Status/Context/Decision/Consequences, Status `Accepted`, name in `docs/adr/NNNN-title.md` form (`skills/docs/scripts/docs_check.py` enforces the shape and unique numbers; 0016 is the highest today - renumber if something else has landed first, and keep the same number in the README and changelog). Record: - Selection is dependency-gated, not wave-gated: a not-done issue whose `dependsOn` are all done is dispatchable regardless of its declared wave, and `wave` becomes a planning hint plus a reporting anchor. - Ownership overlap is resolved by deferral across the in-flight set; a declared same-wave overlap stays a plan defect and is still rejected. - The `documenter` is dispatched alongside the `integrator`; documentation merges only inside a combined GREEN that includes it. - Speculative `specifier` dispatches are permitted and opportunistic; speculative builders are not. - `ownershipHint` is one narrow glob, and issues are split rather than hints widened. - What deliberately stays serial: `specifier` -> `builder` per issue, the integrator's serial merge, nothing merging before combined GREEN, and the two-phase seal. ## Change 2 - `docs/diagrams/src/how-work-moves.json` and the generated SVGs Today the flow is `gate -> merge -> docs -> deploy`, which says documentation happens after the merge. Change it to `pr -> integrator`, `pr -> docs`, `docs -> gate`, `gate -> merge`, `merge -> deploy`: authoring starts from the PRs, and the gate covers the documentation before the orchestrator merges. Keep the node kinds, the group, and the direction; adjust the `docs` node `sub` to say it runs alongside the integrator. Regenerate both themes with `python3 scripts/render-diagrams.py` - editing an SVG by hand does not survive the next run - and keep `--check` green. The renderer's `check_fits` will reject labels that no longer fit; shorten the label rather than widening the diagram. ## Change 3 - `README.md` Update the "How work moves through Workcell" paragraph and the `` text so both match the regenerated picture: the `documenter` is dispatched alongside the `integrator`, its work is covered by the same gate, and the orchestrator merges only on that gate's output. Remove the "then hands the result to `documenter`" sequencing. [ADR 0004](docs/adr/0004-visuals-require-text-equivalents.md) requires the alt text and the nearby prose to carry the same flow as the picture. ## Change 4 - `CHANGELOG.md` One new top entry naming the four changes - dependency-gated scheduling with ownership deferral, the documenter beside the integrator, speculative specifiers, and the ownership-hint granularity rule - and pointing at ADR-0017. ## Change 5 - the assertions Add them to `scripts/tests/test_docs_truth.py`, the existing home for "the docs still say something true" checks, which CI runs via `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`. ## Ownership This issue's hint is `**` on purpose: the pass spans `docs/adr/`, `docs/diagrams/`, the root `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`, and `scripts/tests/`, whose nearest common parent is the repository root. It is the last wave, it is dependency-blocked until everything else has merged, and under this milestone's own deferral rule a repository-wide hint serializes itself. Change only the files named above. ## Verification ```sh python3 -B skills/docs/scripts/docs_check.py . python3 scripts/render-diagrams.py --check python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py' ```

acceptanceTests.oracle: `python3 -B skills/docs/scripts/docs_check.py .` exits 0 with no ADR-numbering or instruction-file-budget violations.

risks.title: A stale speculative seal passes the gate on a moved base
risks.mitigation: The guard binds a seal to its test files and red command, not to the base, so the skill text makes the builder re-prove RED on the merged base before implementing and sends a seal that no longer fails back to a specifier for `tdd-guard reseal --reason`. Speculation stays optional, so the exposure is opt-in.

risks.title: Pull-forward widens the in-flight set past what one integration round can carry
risks.mitigation: waves.py reports the ready set; the skill states the orchestrator may dispatch a subset to cap concurrency, deferral keeps every dispatched pair ownership-disjoint, and the combined-GREEN gate is unchanged.

risks.title: The wave-0 behaviour change surprises an operator or breaks a pinned test
risks.mitigation: test_wave_zero_not_hard_failed is updated in the same issue, the stderr warning is retained, and SKILL.md step 2 states that an overlapping wave-0 pair is now serialized by deferral rather than by hand.

risks.title: A cross-owned contract test blocks an issue that cannot edit it
risks.mitigation: skills/build/tests/test_skill_contracts.py pins phrases in skills the DocumenterOverlap and HintContract issues own. Each issue body lists the phrases it must preserve; a builder that needs one changed stops and escalates instead of writing outside its ownership.

risks.title: The documentation issue owns the whole repository
risks.mitigation: It runs alone in the last wave, is dependency-blocked until every other issue has merged, self-serializes under the new deferral rule, and its acceptance tests name exactly which files must change.

risks.title: ADR 0017 collides with a number landed on another branch
risks.mitigation: docs_check.py rejects duplicate ADR numbers; the issue says to renumber at execution time and to keep the README and changelog citations in step with whatever number is used.

risks.title: The stricter hint rule rejects a sidecar already in flight elsewhere
risks.mitigation: The rule rejects only prose and multi-path values, not coarse-but-valid globs; the single in-tree offender (skills/planner/examples/sample.sidecar.json) is fixed in the same issue, and every other sidecar in the tree already uses one glob per issue.
